novelty.justification: The claim proposes that “transmission strength scales with the overlap between teacher and student empirical NTK / gradient subspaces” and that “aligning two independently initialized models via permutation symmetry (git re-basin) partially restores transmission,” making its novelty route a quantitative mechanism plus a cross-initialization intervention. Searches for “subliminal learning shared initialization gradient alignment,” “subliminal learning neural tangent kernel,” and “re-basin cross-model knowledge transmission” identify Cloud et al. (2025) as the closest phenomenon and theoretical-gradient account, with NTK-based teacher–student alignment already appearing more generally in Supervision Complexity and its Role in Knowledge Distillation (2023), while Git Re-Basin supplies the existing alignment method; the 2026 paper Subliminal Learning is a LoRA Artifact offers a competing mechanism but not this overlap/re-basin hypothesis. Moving from the shared-initialization gradient explanation to an NTK-overlap law is a natural operational extension, whereas proposing function-preserving re-basin alignment as sufficient to reopen the hidden channel is a non-trivial but still compositional adaptation of established machinery rather than a new interpretability paradigm. Together these support standard novelty: no located work is essentially equivalent, but the core direction follows predictably by combining the original paper’s gradient account with existing NTK-alignment and model-rebasining ideas.
